author: Nazmus Sakib Nihal
text:
Advising at NSU is more hectic than anything else, and the ECE Department makes it too hard to get our desired courses as planned. As a result its nearly impossible to finish up all the course within a 4-5 year timeline at NSU for any department, but its possible if we make a proper planning ahead of our semesters.

Here is the breakdown of how I completed my graduation including all the courses from the ECE Department majoring in CSE within 3 years and 8 months timeline! Hopefully it will be helpful for the upcoming freshers who plans to complete the courses within due times. During 2023 and 2024, we had bi-semester system, which later shifted to a tri-semester in 2025 and 2026.

Spring 2023 (13.00 cr)
- CSE115+L, ENG103, MAT116, POL101
Summer 2023 (22.00 cr)
- BEN205, CHE101, CSE173, ENV203, HIS103, MAT120, MAT125, PHY107L
Intersession 2023 (4.00 cr)
- CSE215+L

Spring 2024 (20.00 cr)
- CHE101L, CSE225, CSE231, ECO101, EEE154, HIS102, MAT130, PHY107
Summer 2024 (19.00 cr)
- CSE311, EEE141+L, ENG111, MAT250, PHI104, PHY108

Spring 2025 (16.00 cr)
- CSE327, CSE332, CSE373, EEE111+L, MAT350
Summer 2025 (13.00 cr)
- CSE299, CSE323, CSE482, EEE452, MAT361
Fall 2025 (15.00 cr)
- BIO103, CSE331, CSE425, CSE445, CSE468

Spring 2026 (7.50 cr)
- CSE273, CSE465, CSE499A
Summer 2026 (3.50 cr)
- CSE498R, CSE499B, PHY108L

author: Rn Ahmed Thakur
text:
Course Reviews
I am writing these course reviews cause I needed reviews for cse225, cse231, mat250 and eee141 but there arent any. I see no one writing them anymore so to encourage people I am taking the first step. Also forgive me if I say something out of line and please write reviews everyone, pretty please.
cse215 & cse215L rnn (got A in both)
great teacher, generous grading. sir will give you all the tools and will expect the minimum or the recently taught concept on the quizzes and exams. his question are usually concept driven so its easy. He follows the books with the help of the slides. Effort level was extremely high, lab was tough especially the project. I had to seek a lot of help and somehow had to get away with a bugged code that kept duplicating data in its file.
mat130 ms1 (A-)
rockstar,out of this world, teacher and his questions are not that hard. He tests us conceptually. So even if you dont practice much and understand the math, you can do well. However I messed up in the finals and yet sir curved me to an A minus tho I had done work to deserve that extra credit such as submitting all six assignments and giving all six quizzes etc. Effort level was not consistent, high before mid and low after.
phi104 kis (A)
strict teacher but great for learning. He spoon feeds you the study materials and requires little effort from you however messing up the quizzes will bite you back hard. doesnt curve at all, but is generous in marking in mid and finals. Effort level was low like study before exams.
pol101 nhs1 (A)
engaging and easy going teacher, teaches you what you need to learn and even tells what questions will get on your quizzes. tho writing them essay answers is always hard but if you make your points and give your examples sir gives good marks even if your examples might be a little shaky. Effort level was medium.
phy107 amo (B+)
sir is okay as a teacher, and you can net full marks on your quizzes because everything is from his notes however for mid and final sir doesnt prepare you well for those and sometimes his questions dont match his style of teaching. I gave less effort on this, as he only taught his notes and did not reference other resources plus he tested us on memorization and we all copy pasted his notes as indicated by his questions in the finals however we all did bad in finals. Effort level was medium.
phy107L mmr5 (A)
sir was great and lab instructor was great but course structure was not great tho I had eco101 during most of the course which I later dropped due to pressure. This course ate up every single friday of mine making me write lab reports and prelabs, I hated this course. I would not recommend anyone taking this course with five 3 credit courses. My effort was high as the ceiling of the sistine chapel but I wish I had spent it somewhere else.
Off topic, if you trust me please avoid msk1 for cse173.
Edit-cse225 to 215

text:
Advanced Robotics Workshop: Line follower and Home Automation
A lot of you are already familiar with Arduino and basic robotics, but most of you are probably not using even half of Arduino’s capabilities. Are you ready to upgrade your skillset and put your Arduino programming knowledge into more advanced practical use? NSU ACM Student Chapter is proudly providing you the perfect opportunity to get started through a Workshop on Advanced Robotics.
You have probably noticed that almost every top university in Bangladesh that offers an engineering degree organizes a contest on robotics every year. Most of those contests have segments on the line following robots where the robot has to follow a line and finish the track within the given time. Line following requires you to read sensor data and make decisions based on those data on the fly. Thus, your ability to create an autonomous system is tested. If this piques your interest, then you definitely don’t want to miss this workshop.
But what about situations outside competitions? For ordinary home life, Advanced home automation techniques using the Arduino will also be covered in the workshop. 
We request that you buy the following components required for this workshop:
1.   Arduino UNO / Mega
2.   PVC Board or Car Chassis
3.   Glue Gun with Glue Stick
4.   5 Array IR Sensor
5.   Caster Ball
6.   N20 DC12V 400 Rpm Micro Metal Gear Motor with Wheel
7.   L298N Motor Driver
8.   HC-SR501PIR Motion Detector Module
9.   MQ5 Analog Smoke Sensor
10.   3X4 Flexible Keypad
11.   RFID Module
12.   Mini Servo Motor
13.   L298N Motor Driver
14.   Buzzer
15.   Wires (M-M)- 20 Pieces
16.   Wires (M-F)- 20 Pieces
17.   Ultrasonic Sensor
18.   Breadboard 400 tie pin
19.   Screw Driver (Flat + Star)
20.   1200/1500mah lipo battery
21.   Lipo charger
** You can find the necessary equipments in a package at a reduced price from our partner organization, Robodoc website - http://bit.ly/RD_AR. 
Special Promo code for the workshop - ACMSCRobo102
Please note that, PVC Sheet isn't included in the package. You will have to buy it separately and you can find it in NSU Book Store. 
Registration form: https://forms.gle/uwDt1boQ2fL7J7jf7
Registration deadline: 18th July, 2019
Registration fee:
ACM Members: BDT 100
Non ACM Members: BDT 200
**Bkash transaction Number is provided in the form
 ***If  you do not have any team to attend the workshop together, you can join in and we will set up the teams in first class. Then the teams can buy the package of equipment together.  
Instructors:
The workshop will be taken by our own two experienced instructors who have taken the previous ROBO101 workshops. They are: 
1. Monjurul Islam Uchchahs and 
2. Julhas Hossain
Date: 19th and 26th July, 2nd and 9th August
Time: 10AM-1PM
Venue: LIB606
Prerequisites to attend this workshop: 
Participants are expected to have prior knowledge about basic Robotics(Robo101) since it's an advanced workshop. Also, they are expected to have completed the following courses or have knowledge about these -
1. CSE115(Programming Language I) - C 
2. CSE231 (Digital Logic Design)
3. EEE141 ( Introduction to Circuits) 
4. EEE111(Analog Electronics)
